headline.caveat: 10-year AI hosting agreement for 168MW at Barber Lake (Colorado City, TX), ~$3B contracted revenue; two 5-year extension options lift potential to ~$7B. A Nov 2025 add-on (~39-56MW) added ~$830M more.

realized_to_date.caveat: Delivery due by Sept 2026; early-stage payments/rent not separately disclosed.

nature_md: Fluidstack leases 168MW of critical IT load at Cipher Mining's Barber Lake site in West Texas under a 10-year hosting agreement (~$3B initial term, ~$7B with two 5-year extensions), expanded in Nov 2025 with an additional ~$830M lease. As at TeraWulf, Fluidstack is the tenant serving the Google/Anthropic stack and Google backstops a portion of Fluidstack's obligations, taking Cipher warrants (see related backstop edge). Cipher retains full ownership of the site.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Fluidstack (private) adds multi-billion lease liabilities against end-customer compute demand; its obligations are part-guaranteed by Google, which is what makes Cipher's lenders whole in a default.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Cipher books hosting/lease revenue from service commencement (target Sept 2026) and used the contracted stream plus Google's backstop to raise project financing for the Barber Lake buildout.

events.title: Fluidstack expands Barber Lake lease (~$830M); Google backstop rises to $1.73B
